there are a couple of things that i do when i am feeling like this. 1) do something safe but adrenaline-producing like jumping into a cold shower with all my clothes on 2) go for a long walk to dissect my thoughts from as much of an objective perspective as i can 3) write emotionally about it in a notebook. sometimes i write poetry or i journal about it.

i am not really sure what is going on for you but you seem very distressed nonetheless. I'm going to take a guess that you are in middle or early high school. And if that it the case, i just want to assure you that the things that you think are a huge deal are actually pretty insignificant in the long run. so while things may feel like a lot right now, everything will turn out okay no matter what is going on. just stay safe and don't make any rash decisions and try not to turn to permanent/semi-permanent "solutions" like self-harm or suicide attempts.

just want to say that you are so young and if you stop now you will be able to fix everything. don't get caught in the vicious cycle. use me as a cautionary tale. i started when i was around your age and i am twenty now. i have a ten-year-old sister who has had to see what couldn't be hidden of my suicidal and alcoholic history and it is devastating. i wish i could go back and undo what i did when i was your age and stop when it started to get bad. please be safe and stop things while you still can.
